what: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by the E20 lane, building the mechanism the manager specified after the operator asked what was being done about three silent-check incidents. [!] THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT FIRST, BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS FIX CONTAINS A REGRESS THIS REPO HAS ALREADY PAID FOR: 'make every check emit a receipt and have something grade receipt freshness' IS ALREADY BUILT -- scripts/ci/check_manager_queue_watch.py is exactly that design, and the Routine it grades has fired ~479 times in 479 hours and written ZERO receipts. The receipt-grader was itself the thing that never ran, so adding receipts moves the silence up one level and asks who watches the watcher. THE WAY OUT IS A DIFFERENT SUBSTRATE, not a better timer: a scheduled job can always be the thing that did not fire and its not-firing is invisible by construction, while CI runs on every push, so CI's own liveness is PROVEN BY THE FACT THAT PRs MERGE AT ALL. [!] WHAT WAS BUILT: scripts/ci/check_cadence_liveness.py, WIRED into run_guards.py as `cadence-liveness` (when: None, self-test first). The POPULATION IS DERIVED FROM THE TREE, never hand-maintained -- a check that never registers would be invisible again, same bug new clothes -- from `.github/workflows/*.yml` carrying `on.schedule.cron` and from `deploy/*.timer` carrying `OnCalendar=`. ANYTHING DERIVED AND UNREGISTERED FAILS; that is the omission-detectable property and it is the structural half. Six states never collapsed: fresh / stale / never_ran / schedule_unknown / no_receipt / unregistered. [!] THE MEASUREMENT, and it is the number the operator needs to choose what becomes blocking: POPULATION 38 in-repo cadence declarations -- 18 of 143 workflows carry a `schedule:`, plus 20 deploy/*.timer units (11 with a readable OnCalendar, 9 triggered by another unit and so declaring no calendar of their own, which is schedule_unknown rather than a fault). RESULT: fresh 1, stale 0, never_ran 0, schedule_unknown 0, no_receipt 37, unregistered 0. [!] SO EXACTLY ONE OF THIRTY-EIGHT SCHEDULED THINGS CAN CURRENTLY BE SEEN TO HAVE RUN (trainer-capture-watch.yml, which commits docs/claude/work/TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH.json back to main, so its last commit IS the receipt and no new artifact was needed). The other 37 are ungradeable, and that is REPORTED as its own count rather than folded into `fresh` -- folding it would make the module commit the defect it exists to find, and at 37 of 38 it is the largest bucket by far. [!] THE 37 SPLIT INTO TWO TRACTABILITY TIERS, which is what makes this actionable rather than a lament: 8 more scheduled workflows already COMMIT BACK (measured by grepping commit-to-main / git push across the 18), so each is ONE DECLARED OUTPUT PATH away from being gradeable with no cooperation from the workflow at all -- that is the cheap shrink. The remaining 9 workflows leave no in-repo trace (their history is in the Actions API, which this guard deliberately does not call: a guard that needs the network reds on an outage), and all 20 timers run ON THE VM where nothing they do reaches this repo, so the diag relays are their surface rather than CI. [!] THE RESIDUAL, NAMED IN THE GUARD'S STANDING DISCLOSURE AND PRINTED ON EVERY RUN INCLUDING CLEAN ONES: A ROUTINE IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE REPOSITORY. Routines live in the Claude Code Remote API, which CI cannot reach, so the omission of a Routine is NOT detected -- and instance #3 of this class WAS a Routine. This guard covers the IN-REPO half of the class and no more, and says so rather than implying completeness. Closing the other half needs a receipt a Routine-fired session can actually write, which today it cannot, because those sessions get neither a repo checkout nor any mcp__ tool. [!] REPORT-FIRST ON PURPOSE, and the trap was stated by the manager before I could walk into it: 38 red entries on day one gets the guard reverted and then there is nothing. The day-one population is carried in a dated BASELINE that may only SHRINK with the counts printed every run; only an UNREGISTERED new cadence, a newly stale graded receipt, or baseline rot (an entry that recovered, or whose source file is gone) fails. `--strict` fails on the debt too. What becomes blocking beyond those is the operator's call, not this module's. Self-test 25 cases including the DERIVATION CONTROL (a workflow with no `schedule:` must not enter the population) and the refusals (an unparseable cron returns None rather than a guessed interval -- a fabricated threshold under a freshness verdict is the same defect as a fabricated $0 under a cost).
